review: 1:1 עָלָה אָדוֹן אֶל־אָבִיו — the ascension is stated with עָלָה, the verb of Ps 68:19 and Eph 4:8, which is why no 'into heaven' is needed.
3:3 זֵכֶר שֵׁם — 'the remembrance of the Name'; the Arabic ذِكْرُ اسْمِ is a construct, and Hebrew keeps the double construct rather than saying 'mentioning'.
4:4 הוּא יְקַיֵּם הַבְטָחָה — 'He will fulfil the promise'; the Arabic سَيُنْجِزُ الْوَعْدَ is the same future certainty, kept as a verbless emphatic clause.
5:1–5:2 יָקִים ... יְשַׁנֶּה — 'He will raise from beneath the dust, He will change our bodies'; the two verbs are the resurrection sequence of 1 Cor 15:52 and Phil 3:21.
5:3–5:4 יַחְטֹף ... וְלֹא נִרְאֶה — 'He will snatch us away and we shall not see death or decay'; the Arabic يَخْطَفُنَا is 1 Thess 4:17, and חָטַף is the biblical verb for snatching (Judg 21:21).
